mainTopic: Stories of prayer for rain: why some leaders were answered at once and others were not, ending with the greatness of רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
overview: This amud is a chain of stories about praying for rain. It opens with רבה answering people who asked why his fast failed when רב יהודה's fasts brought rain. He says it cannot be learning, since his generation learns far more, and not his own deeds; the generation itself is unworthy. The גמרא then tells how רב יהודה caused a famine with an angry look, and later, when he removed one shoe to fast, rain fell at once. רבא's fast in הגרוניא is answered after a dream shows an עת רצון. Later, to answer שבור מלכא's test, רבא brings summer rain but is warned in a dream that pressing Heaven so hard is dangerous. רב פפא's rain comes only when he is embarrassed and humbled. רבי חנינא בן דוסא stops and restarts the rain with one sentence, and רב יוסף notes that this outweighs even the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים prayer against travelers' prayers. The amud ends by praising רבי חנינא's poverty and begins a story about his wife, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה's generation studied mainly נזיקין, while we study all six סדרים
steps.stepSummary: רבה continues his complaint: in רב יהודה's day, learning centered on נזיקין, but now everyone learns all of ששה סדרי משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [All the learning in רב יהודה's years] was in נזיקין, and we learn all six סדרים.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of רבה's speech. He compares how much Torah was learned in רב יהודה's generation with how much is learned in his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is answering a challenge put to him on the previous amud: 'רב יהודה's fasts brought rain, so why not yours?' He first shows that learning cannot be the reason, because his generation actually covers more ground than רב יהודה's did.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the משנה dealing with damages and civil law
The six orders of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins mid-sentence. The speaker is רבה, explaining why his fast for rain was not answered even though his generation learns more Torah.

phrases.english: was in Nezikin (the order of damages),
phrases.notes: Completes a sentence begun on the previous amud: 'all the learning in רב יהודה's years...'

phrases.english: and we learn all six orders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's speech earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earlier generations studied less Torah than רבה's generation.

steps.title: רב יהודה found עוקצין as hard as the disputes of רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: When רב יהודה reached the difficult material in עוקצין, he said it felt like the hardest disputes of רב ושמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יהודה reached עוקצין, at 'a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot' (some say: 'olives pickled with their leaves are pure'), he would say: 'I see the disputes of רב ושמואל here!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives an example of how hard certain מסכתות were for רב יהודה's generation. Even רב יהודה found עוקצין extremely difficult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two quoted משניות are given as alternate versions (ואמרי לה) of where רב יהודה would get stuck. Calling it 'הוויות דרב ושמואל' means it seemed as complex as the toughest debates of those two אמוראים. The point is that this material was beyond their usual learning.

keyTerms.meaning: מסכת עוקצין, dealing with stems and fruit and impurity; considered very difficult

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין
phrases.english: And when Rav Yehuda would reach Uktzin
('a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot'),
phrases.notes: Quoting a משנה (טהרות 2:1)

phrases.english: and some say: ('olives pickled with their leaves are pure'),
phrases.notes: עוקצין 2:1

phrases.english: he would say: the disputes of Rav and Shmuel
I see here,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the earlier generation's more limited learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוקצין was extremely difficult for רב יהודה.

steps.title: We learn more, yet only רב יהודה was answered at once
steps.stepSummary: רבה's generation learns עוקצין in thirteen yeshivos. Yet רב יהודה got rain after removing one shoe, while they cry all day and no one notices.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learn עוקצין in thirteen yeshivos. Yet רב יהודה, when he took off one shoe, the rain came, and we cry out all day and nobody pays attention to us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes the learning part of his answer. His generation knows more Torah, so learning cannot be why רב יהודה was answered instantly while they are ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would expect more Torah learning to bring more merit, yet the facts show the opposite. So learning is not what makes the difference. רבה now turns to the other possibility, deeds, in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנַן קָא מַתְנֵינַן בְּעוּקְצִין תְּלֵיסַר מְתִיבָתָא.
phrases.english: And we learn Uktzin in thirteen yeshivot.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ רַב יְהוּדָה, כִּי הֲוָה שָׁלֵיף חַד מְסָאנָא —
phrases.english: Yet Rav Yehuda, when he would remove one shoe,
phrases.notes: Taking off shoes was a sign of fasting and distress.

phrases.english: the rain would come,
and we cry out all day
and there is no one who notices us.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ רַב יְהוּדָה, כִּי הֲוָה שָׁלֵיף חַד מְסָאנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast: more learning, yet fewer answered prayers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that more Torah learning brings quicker answers to prayer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה's generation learns more than רב יהודה's, yet only רב יהודה was answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning cannot explain the difference, since רבה's generation learns more, yet רב יהודה was answered at once while they are ignored.

steps.title: The fault lies with the generation, not its leaders
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that if anyone saw him do something wrong, let him say so. Otherwise, the great leaders cannot help when the generation itself is unworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of deeds, if anyone saw me do something wrong, let him say it. But what can the great ones of the generation do when their generation is not worthy?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers his own puzzle. The problem is not his learning or his conduct, but the conduct of the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה rules out his own deeds by inviting anyone to accuse him. He concludes that even righteous leaders cannot bring rain when the generation as a whole does not deserve it.

keyTerms.meaning: The great leaders of the generation

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's message: a generation's merit, not only its leaders' Torah, decides whether prayers are answered.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the community's behavior affects whether prayers like the תענית for rain are answered.

phrases.english: If it is because of deeds,
if there is anyone who saw anything (wrong in me), let him say so,
but what can the great ones of the generation do
when their generation is not worthy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out learning in steps 1–3, רבה rules out his own deeds and puts the blame on the generation, completing his answer to the challenge from the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lack of rain is due to the generation's unworthiness, not its leaders' failings.

steps.title: רב יהודה sees bread wasted and causes a famine
steps.stepSummary: The story behind the shoe begins: רב יהודה saw two people throwing bread around, concluded there was too much plenty, looked angrily, and a famine came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה saw two people throwing bread at each other. He said: 'This shows there is plenty in the world.' He set his eyes on it, and there was a famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the story behind 'רב יהודה removed one shoe.' This first part explains how a famine started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wasting bread showed disrespect for food. רב יהודה concluded people had too much. His angry look had so much power that it brought a famine.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה חֲזָא הָנְהוּ בֵּי תְרֵי
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda saw a certain two people
who were throwing (wasting) bread,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אִיכָּא שִׂבְעָא בְּעָלְמָא,
phrases.english: he said: learn from this that there is plenty in the world,
he cast his eyes, and there was a famine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה חֲזָא הָנְהוּ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story that explains the shoe mentioned in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's anger at wasted bread brought a famine.

steps.title: The Rabbis have his attendant lead him past the market
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן asked רב כהנא, רב יהודה's attendant, to get him to leave by the door near the market so he would see the famine. He did, and רב יהודה saw a crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב כהנא son of רב נחוניא, his attendant: 'You are often with him. Persuade him to go out by the door near the market.' He persuaded him, he went out to the market, and he saw a crowd.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars make a plan to show רב יהודה how bad the famine has become, hoping he will pray for it to end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה apparently did not know the effect his look had caused. Only someone close to him could change his route without upsetting him, so the רבנן turned to his attendant.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is often in his presence

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Kahana
son of Rav Neḥunya, his attendant:
Master, who is often before him,
should persuade him to go out
by the door that is near the market.
He persuaded him and he went out to the market,
he saw a crowd,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the famine leads the רבנן to act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן arrange for רב יהודה to see the famine for himself.

steps.title: A crowd over one basket of dates shows the famine
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asked what the crowd was. They said they were standing by a basket of dates for sale. He concluded there was a famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'What is this?' They said: 'We are standing by a basket of dates that is being sold.' He said: 'This shows there is a famine in the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה finds out why people are crowding and realizes how severe the famine is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So many people crowding around one small basket of dates proves food is very scarce. This mirrors step 5: there he used 'שמע מינה' to conclude there was plenty, and here he uses it to conclude there is famine.

phrases.english: He said to them: What is this?
They said to him: we are standing by a basket of dates
that is being sold.
He said: learn from this that there is famine in the world,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה asks about the crowd he saw in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה realizes there is a famine.

steps.title: He removes one shoe and rain falls
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה told his attendant to remove his shoes as a sign of fasting. After one shoe came off, rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his attendant: 'Take off my shoes.' He took off one shoe, and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה begins a fast to end the famine, and the rain comes immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking off shoes is a sign of mourning and fasting. The rain came before he even finished, which is the 'one shoe' רבה described in step 3.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: שְׁלוֹף לִי מְסָאנַיי.
phrases.english: He said to his attendant: remove my shoes.
He removed one shoe for him
and rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: שְׁלוֹף לִי מְסָאנַיי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה acts on his realization that there is a famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's fast was answered immediately.

steps.title: אליהו warns him not to remove the second shoe
steps.stepSummary: As he began to remove the second shoe, אליהו came and said in the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא: if you remove the other one, I will destroy the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came to take off the other shoe, אליהו came and said to him: 'הקדוש ברוך הוא says: if you take off the other one, I will destroy the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a heavenly warning showing how powerful רב יהודה's distress was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's pain mattered so much in heaven that his further suffering would bring a drastic response. This proves רבה's point: in רב יהודה's time prayer was answered at once, unlike in רבה's generation.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'one shoe' story shows how instantly רב יהודה's prayers were answered, the backdrop for רבה's complaint about his own generation.

phrases.english: When he came to remove the other one,
Elijah came and said to him:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
If you remove the other one,
I will destroy the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the shoe story begun in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה's distress was so powerful in heaven that removing the second shoe would bring destruction.

steps.title: רב מרי Sees Angels Turn Sand into Flour
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי, the son of שמואל's daughter, describes how he saw angels disguised as sailors fill boats with sand that turned into fine flour. He told people not to buy it, because miracle food should not be used and real wheat would arrive the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of שמואל's daughter, said: I was standing on the bank of נהר פפא. I saw angels who looked like sailors bringing sand and filling ships with it, and it became fine flour. Everyone came to buy it. I said to them: Do not buy from this, because it is the product of miracles. Tomorrow, ships of wheat will come from פרזינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an eyewitness account from the famine story of רב יהודה. רב מרי saw a miracle that produced flour, but he told people not to buy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The famine ended in a miraculous way, and רב מרי saw the miracle itself. Even so, he would not let people benefit from it, because one should not get pleasure from a מעשה נסים when natural food is about to arrive. He knew regular wheat boats from פרזינא would come the next day.
steps.confusionAlert: רב מרי is not saying the flour was forbidden or impure. He only discourages using food that came from a miracle when natural food is coming soon.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Shmuel's daughter, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא אַגּוּדָּא דִּנְהַר פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: I was standing on the bank of the Pappa River,
I saw angels who looked like sailors
who were bringing sand and filling ships with it,
and it became fine flour.
Everyone came to buy it.
I said to them: Do not buy from this,
phrases.notes: He was warning people not to benefit from food made by a miracle.

phrases.english: because it is the product of miracles.
Tomorrow, ships of wheat will come from Parzina.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an eyewitness report about how the famine of רב יהודה's time ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should avoid benefiting from a miracle when natural food is about to arrive.

steps.title: רבא Decrees a Fast in Hagrunya but No Rain Comes
steps.stepSummary: רבא visits הגרוניא and decrees a fast, but no rain falls. He tells everyone to keep fasting overnight. The next morning he asks whether anyone had a dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא happened to come to הגרוניא. He decreed a fast, but rain did not come. He said to them: Everyone, continue your fast through the night. The next day he said to them: Whoever saw a dream, let him say it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rain story begins. This step sets up the next move: רבא is looking for a sign from Heaven through a dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first fast did not bring rain, so רבא did not stop. He extended the fast overnight. Then he asked for dreams, hoping someone had received a message about whether their prayers would be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: stay overnight in your fast; keep fasting through the night

phrases.english: Rava happened to come to Hagrunya.
He decreed a fast, but rain did not come.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: בִּיתוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּתַעֲנִיתַיְיכוּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: Everyone, continue your fast through the night.
The next day he said to them:
Whoever saw a dream, let him say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about praying for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a fast does not bring rain, the community keeps fasting and looks for a sign from Heaven.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר Reports a Dream of Good Greetings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר of הגרוניא reports that in his dream he heard: 'Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord, Who in His goodness does good for His people.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר of הגרוניא said to them: This was read to me in my dream: Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord, Who in His goodness does good for His people.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone answers רבא's question and tells his dream. The dream contains a message of goodness from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dream uses the word 'good' (טב) again and again: good greetings, a good master, a good Lord. The 'good master' is רבא, and the 'good Lord' is הקדוש ברוך הוא. This suggests Heaven is ready to do good for the people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar of Hagrunya said to them:
This was read to me in my dream:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלָם טָב לְרַב טָב מֵרִיבּוֹן טָב,
phrases.english: Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord,
Who in His goodness does good for His people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's request for anyone who had a dream.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dream sends a message of Heavenly goodness toward רבא and the people.

steps.title: רבא Understands It Is a Favorable Time, Prays, and Rain Comes
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes from the dream that this is an עת רצון, a favorable time to pray. They pray, and rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn from this that it is a favorable time to pray for mercy. They prayed for mercy, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what the dream means, and the story ends with success: rain falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the dream as a sign that Heaven is open to prayer right now. He acts on it immediately, and the prayer is answered. This closes the הגרוניא story.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this; we can conclude
a favorable time, when prayer is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: A sign from Heaven can show that it is an עת רצון, a time when prayer will be accepted, and acting at that moment brings results.

phrases.english: He said: Learn from this
that it is a favorable time (to pray for mercy).
phrases.notes: The words in parentheses are a textual addition that explains the meaning.

phrases.english: They prayed for mercy, and rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the dream from the previous step and brings the story to its end.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dream showed it was an עת רצון; they prayed and rain fell.

steps.title: A Man Dies from Lashes in רבא's Court and the King Wants to Punish רבא
steps.stepSummary: A man is sentenced to lashes in רבא's court for relations with a non-Jewish woman. He dies from the lashes. When King שבור hears about it, he wants to punish רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man was sentenced to lashes in רבא's court because he had relations with a gentile woman. רבא had him flogged, and he died. The matter was heard in the house of שבור מלכא, and he wanted to punish רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. This step sets up the danger to רבא, which leads to the rain challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man died from the punishment. In the king's eyes, this looked as if רבא had carried out a death penalty without royal permission. So שבור מלכא wanted to make רבא suffer for it.

phrases.english: A certain man who was sentenced to lashes
in Rava's court
because he had relations with a gentile woman.
Rava had him flogged, and he died.
The matter was heard in the house of King Shapur,
and he wanted to punish Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאִיחַיַּיב נְגָדָא בְּבֵי דִינָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that will also involve praying for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא is in danger from the Persian king after a man dies under the punishment of his court.

steps.title: The King's Mother Warns Him Not to Fight the Jews
steps.stepSummary: איפרא הורמיז, the mother of שבור מלכא, tells her son not to quarrel with the Jews, because whatever they ask from their Master, He gives them.
steps.simpleTranslation: איפרא הורמיז, the mother of שבור מלכא, said to her son: Do not get into any dispute with the Jews, because whatever they ask from their Master, He gives them.
steps.whatsHappening: The king's mother steps in to protect רבא. She warns her son that the Jews have a special connection to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her argument is that fighting the Jews is dangerous, because God answers their requests. This claim is what the king will now question and test.

keyTerms.meaning: a dispute, getting involved with someone

phrases.english: Ifra Hormiz said to him,
the mother of King Shapur, to her son:
Do not get into any dispute
with the Jews,
because whatever they ask from their Master
He gives them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ אִיפְרָא הוֹרְמִיז אִימֵּיהּ דְּשַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא לִבְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the king's plan to punish רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God answers the requests of the Jews, so it is dangerous to fight them.

steps.title: The King Asks for an Example
steps.stepSummary: שבור מלכא asks his mother what she means: what does God give the Jews?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The king asks his mother for proof of her claim. This sets up her answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He wants a concrete example that shows God answers the Jews. This question opens a short exchange of question, answer, and challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? what do you mean?

phrases.english: He said to her: What is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the mother's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: An example of God granting the Jews' requests.

steps.title: The Mother Answers: They Pray and Rain Comes
steps.stepSummary: The king's mother answers that when the Jews pray for mercy, rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: She replied: They pray for mercy, and rain comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The mother gives her example: the Jews' prayers bring rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her proof is that rain answers their prayers. This proof is easy to attack, and the king attacks it in the next step.

phrases.english: They pray for mercy, and rain comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the king's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their prayers for rain are answered.

steps.title: The King Objects: That Is Just the Rainy Season
steps.stepSummary: שבור מלכא rejects the proof, saying the rain falls only because it is the rainy season. He demands that the Jews pray now, in the summer season of תמוז, and that rain come then.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: That happens because it is the season for rain. Rather, let them pray for mercy now, in the season of תמוז, and let rain come.
steps.whatsHappening: The king challenges his mother's proof. He sets a harder test: rain in the middle of summer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His attack is that rain during the rainy season proves nothing, because it would have rained anyway. Only rain in תמוז, when it normally does not rain in Babylonia, would show that God truly answers prayer.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a halachic קשיא. It is the king's objection inside the story, but it works like a challenge: it attacks the proof that was just given.

phrases.english: He said to her: That
is because it is the season for rain.
Rather, let them pray for mercy now,
in the season of Tammuz, and let rain come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the mother's proof as natural coincidence.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that rain after prayer proves God answers the Jews.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain in the rainy season happens naturally, so only rain out of season would be real proof.

steps.title: רבא Prays for Summer Rain, but None Comes at First
steps.stepSummary: איפרא הורמיז sends a message to רבא asking him to focus and pray for rain. רבא prays, but rain does not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: She sent a message to רבא: Focus your mind and pray for mercy so that rain will come. He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The test begins. רבא prays, but at first there is no rain, which sets up what will happen next in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother wants to prove her point, so she asks רבא to pray with full concentration. His first prayer fails, which raises the tension. The story continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: she sent a message to him

steps.confusionAlert: The story is not over. Do not assume רבא's prayer failed for good; Step 20 tells how his second prayer brought a huge rain.

phrases.english: She sent a message to Rava:
Focus your mind and pray for mercy
so that rain will come.
He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחָה לֵיהּ לְרָבָא: כַּוֵּין דַּעְתָּךְ וּבְעִי רַחֲמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the king's test from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's first prayer for summer rain is not answered, which sets up the continuation of the story.

steps.title: רבא's prayer is answered with a huge rain
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a פסוק from תהלים, complaining that we have only heard about God's miracles and never seen them. A huge rain comes right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before God: Master of the Universe! 'O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers have told us, of the work You did in their days, in days of old.' But we have not seen it with our own eyes! Rain came until the gutters of מחוזא poured into the Tigris.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the story from the last step. רבא's first prayer did not work, so now he prays again in a bolder way, and this time it rains so hard that the city's gutters overflow into the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses a פסוק to argue with God: the earlier generations were told about miracles, but our generation has never seen one. This bold argument works. The rain is so strong that it clearly answers the king's challenge that rain only falls in its season.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the Universe, a way of speaking directly to God
מחוזא, the city in Babylonia where רבא lived

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבא, continuing from the previous step.

phrases.english: "O God, we have heard with our ears,
phrases.notes: Quoting תהלים 44:2.

phrases.english: our fathers have told us
of the work You did in their days, in days of old"
but we have not seen it with our own eyes!
phrases.notes: רבא's own addition to the פסוק. This is the heart of his request.

phrases.english: Rain came
until the gutters of Mechoza poured into the Tigris.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא tries a second time after his first prayer failed, and this time it succeeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's bold prayer, built on the פסוק, brings a miraculous summer rain that answers שבור מלכא's challenge.

steps.title: רבא's father warns him in a dream
steps.stepSummary: רבא's late father appears to him in a dream. He scolds רבא for pushing Heaven so hard, and tells him to sleep somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father came and appeared to him in his dream, and said to him: Is there anyone who troubles Heaven this much? He said to him: Change your place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that the miracle had a cost. רבא's father tells him he has "bothered" Heaven too much and warns him to move his bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for rain out of its season was seen as pressing Heaven very hard. That kind of demand can bring danger on the person who makes it. The father's advice is protection: get away from the place where harm is waiting.

phrases.english: His father came and appeared to him in his dream
and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא דְּמַיטְרַח קַמֵּי שְׁמַיָּא כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: Is there anyone who troubles Heaven this much?
phrases.notes: A rebuke: you should not have pushed so hard.

phrases.english: He said to him: Change your place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after the miracle, the story turns to its dangerous result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forcing Heaven's hand, even with success, puts the one who prays in danger.

steps.title: רבא's bed is found slashed by knives
steps.stepSummary: רבא follows his father's advice. The next day he finds his old bed cut up by knives.
steps.simpleTranslation: He changed his place. The next day he found that his bed had been slashed with knives.
steps.whatsHappening: This ends the רבא story. The warning was real: if רבא had slept in his usual bed, he would have been hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slashed bed proves that the danger his father spoke about was real, and that listening to the dream saved רבא. The story praises how powerful רבא's prayer was, but it also teaches caution about demanding miracles.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's prayer brought a summer rain, but his father warned him that troubling Heaven so much was dangerous, and the slashed bed proved it.

phrases.english: He changed his place;
the next day he found it
that his bed had been slashed with knives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened after רבא followed the dream's instruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger was real, and moving his bed saved רבא.

steps.title: רב פפא's fast and prayer bring no rain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא declares a fast for rain, but no rain comes. Feeling weak, he eats a bowl of porridge and then prays, and still no rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא declared a fast, and rain did not come. He felt faint, so he swallowed a bowl of porridge and prayed for mercy, and rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rain story begins. רב פפא does everything expected of a leader, a public fast and prayer, but nothing happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא ate while the community was fasting, because he felt too weak to continue. His prayer still does not work. This sets up the next steps, which show what finally did bring the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: His heart became weak (he felt faint from hunger)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa declared a fast
and rain did not come.
His heart grew weak,
he swallowed a bowl of porridge
and prayed for mercy
and rain did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate story about praying for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא's fast and prayer did not bring rain.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר אושפזתי mocks רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר אושפזתי makes a sarcastic remark: if you eat another bowl of porridge, the rain will come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר אושפזתי said to him: If the master swallows another bowl of porridge, rain will come.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone pokes fun at רב פפא for eating during the fast, hinting that this is why the rain is not coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remark is mockery, not real advice. It points out that a leader who eats during a public fast cannot expect his prayers to work. This sets up the next step, where the embarrassment itself changes things.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a polite title for a חכם

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as real advice to eat more. It is sarcasm aimed at רב פפא for eating during the fast.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אוּשְׁפַּזְתִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Ushpazti said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי שָׂרֵיף מָר פִּינְכָּא אַחֲרִיתִי דְּדַיְיסָא
phrases.english: If the master swallows another bowl of porridge
rain will come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אוּשְׁפַּזְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A mocking reaction to רב פפא eating during the fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא is mocked for eating during the public fast.

steps.title: רב פפא is humbled and rain comes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא feels ashamed and upset, and then the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was embarrassed and became upset, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: This ends the רב פפא story. His fast and prayer did not bring rain, but his shame and broken spirit did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What changed was רב פפא's inner state, not his actions. A humbled heart brought the rain that his formal fast could not. The lesson is that a broken, humble spirit is valued in Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: His spirit was weakened (he felt upset, humbled)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's rain came because of his humility and embarrassment, not because of his fast.

phrases.english: He was embarrassed, and became upset,
and rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mockery causes the humility that finally brings the rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humility, not the fast itself, brought the rain.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן דוסא stops the rain on the road
steps.stepSummary: While רבי חנינא בן דוסא is traveling, it starts to rain. He tells God that everyone else is comfortable while he suffers, and the rain stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was walking on the road, and rain came. He said before God: Master of the Universe, the whole world is comfortable, and חנינא is suffering! The rain stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: Another rain story begins. רבי חנינא בן דוסא, getting wet on the road, simply tells God how he feels, and the rain stops at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבא and רב פפא, רבי חנינא needs no fast and no special effort. A few plain words are enough to stop the rain. This shows how close and powerful his relationship with God was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa
was walking along the road,
rain came.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
the entire world is comfortable,
phrases.notes: Everyone else is happy, because they need the rain.

phrases.english: and Chanina is suffering!
The rain stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rain story, about a צדיק whose prayer works instantly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's short words immediately stop the rain.

steps.title: At home, רבי חנינא brings the rain back
steps.stepSummary: When רבי חנינא reaches home, he tells God that now the whole world is suffering while he is comfortable, and the rain comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he arrived home, he said before God: Master of the Universe, the whole world is suffering, and חנינא is comfortable? Rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: This ends the story. Now that רבי חנינא is safe at home, he asks for the rain everyone needs, and it comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same simple words, turned around, bring the rain back. רבי חנינא could turn the rain on and off almost at will. This leads straight into רב יוסף's comment in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן דוסא could stop and restart the rain with a single sentence.

phrases.english: When he arrived at his home,
he said before Him: Master of the Universe,
the entire world is suffering
and Chanina is comfortable?
Rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of the previous step: the rain is brought back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא's word brings the rain back as easily as it stopped it.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the כהן גדול's prayer is no match for רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what good the כהן גדול's prayer could do against the prayer of רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What help is the prayer of the כהן גדול compared to רבי חנינא בן דוסא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reacts to the רבי חנינא story. His point is that even the כהן גדול's prayer, said on the holiest day in the holiest place, could be outweighed by רבי חנינא's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא stopped rain that the world needed. The כהן גדול prayed for rain on יום הכפורים, yet one personal request from רבי חנינא could override it. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא brings the source showing what the כהן גדול prayed.

keyTerms.meaning: What did it help? What effect did it have?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ צְלוֹתָא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: What effect does the prayer of the High Priest have
against Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי אַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ צְלוֹתָא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A comment on the רבי חנינא story, comparing it to the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא's prayer can outweigh even the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים prayer.

steps.title: The משנה: the כהן גדול's short prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a משנה: the כהן גדול would say a short prayer in the outer chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: He would pray a short prayer in the outer chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings the source for his comment. The משנה tells us that the כהן גדול said a short prayer after leaving the קדש הקדשים on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה proves that the כהן גדול had a special prayer, which רב יוסף is comparing to רבי חנינא's. It does not yet tell us what the prayer said, so the גמרא asks about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The outer chamber (the היכל, outside the קדש הקדשים)

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
He would pray a short prayer
in the outer chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the כהן גדול's prayer that רב יוסף mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן גדול said a special prayer on יום הכפורים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יומא about the short prayer in the outer chamber

steps.title: What did the כהן גדול pray?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words of the כהן גדול's short prayer were.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would he pray?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what exactly did the כהן גדול say? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says that the prayer was short. To understand רב יוסף's comparison, we need to know its words, which turn out to be about rain.

phrases.english: What would he pray?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the prayer the משנה mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the כהן גדול's short prayer

steps.title: The prayer: may this year be rainy and hot
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר אדא and רבא בר אדא, quoting רב יהודה, say the prayer was: May it be Your will that this year be rainy and hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר אדא and רבא בר אדא both said in the name of רב יהודה: May it be Your will, Lord our God, that this year be rainy and hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The כהן גדול prayed for a year with plenty of rain and heat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the כהן גדול's prayer was about rain, which explains רב יוסף's comparison with רבי חנינא. But the word "hot" is surprising, and the next step questions it.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִין בַּר אַדָּא וְרָבָא בַּר אַדָּא
phrases.english: Ravin bar Adda and Rava bar Adda
both said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that this year shall be
rainy and hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִין בַּר אַדָּא וְרָבָא בַּר אַדָּא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about what the prayer said.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The prayer asked that the year be rainy and hot.

steps.title: Why would anyone pray for heat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: heat is not a blessing, it is the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is heat something good? On the contrary, it is something bad!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the word "hot" in the prayer. Why would the כהן גדול ask for something harmful? Step 33 gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heat seems to dry crops and hurt people, so asking for it looks strange in a prayer for blessing. The challenge targets that one word, not the whole prayer. The גמרא will need to explain how heat can be part of a good year.

phrases.english: Is heat a good thing?
On the contrary, it is a bad thing!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחוּנָה מְעַלַּיְיתָא הִיא? אַדְּרַבָּה, גְּרִיעוּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one word in the prayer quoted in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word שחונה (hot) in the כהן גדול's prayer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heat is harmful, so it makes no sense to ask for it in a prayer for blessing.

steps.title: Corrected wording: if the year is hot, let it also be rainy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the prayer. The כהן גדול did not ask for heat. He asked that if the year turns out hot, it should also be rainy and moist.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the prayer was: If the year is hot, let it be rainy and moist with dew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 32 by changing the wording of the prayer. Heat is no longer something requested. It is a condition that might happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that heat is not a blessing. The fix is that the כהן גדול never asked for heat. He said: if You decided the year will be hot, at least send rain and dew so the crops are not harmed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as the כהן גדול praying for heat. The word אִם ("if") turns heat into a possibility he is guarding against.

phrases.english: Rather: if it is hot
phrases.notes: אֶלָּא signals that the earlier wording is being replaced

phrases.english: let it be rainy and moist with dew.
phrases.notes: Rain and dew protect the crops from the heat

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 32 by rewording the prayer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prayer asked for a year that is both rainy and hot.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prayer only says: if the year is hot, let it also be rainy and moist.

steps.title: The key line: do not accept the prayer of travelers
steps.stepSummary: The prayer continues: the כהן גדול asked ה׳ not to accept the prayer of travelers. This is the line that completes רב יוסף's proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let the prayer of travelers not come before You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next line of the כהן גדול's prayer. This is the line רב יוסף was building toward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Travelers pray for the rain to stop so their trip is not ruined. The כהן גדול asked ה׳ to ignore those prayers, because the world needs rain. Yet רבי חנינא בן דוסא prayed as a traveler and the rain stopped. That shows his prayer was stronger than the כהן גדול's.

keyTerms.meaning: Enter before You, be accepted by You

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the point of the whole discussion that began in Step 28. It explains why רב יוסף said the כהן גדול's prayer could do nothing against רבי חנינא בן דוסא.

phrases.english: And let not enter before You
phrases.notes: A request that ה׳ not accept something

phrases.english: the prayer of travelers.
phrases.notes: Travelers pray against rain, but the world needs rain

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל יִכָּנֵס לְפָנֶיךָ תְּפִילַּת עוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the prayer and reaches the line that proves רב יוסף's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the כהן גדול's prayer could not override רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer
steps.raayaSupportSource: The כהן גדול's request that travelers' prayers not be accepted, compared with the story of רבי חנינא בן דוסא stopping the rain while traveling

steps.title: An added ending to the prayer: rule for יהודה and no dependence on others
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא, quoting רב יהודה, adds the closing words: may rulership not leave the house of יהודה, and may כלל ישראל not need to depend on each other or on another nation for a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא concluded the prayer in the name of רב יהודה: May the ruler not depart from the house of יהודה, and may Your people ישראל not need to be supported by one another, nor by another nation.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives the final lines of the כהן גדול's prayer. This adds to the wording already quoted; it does not argue with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part asks that Jewish leadership continue. The second part asks for a good economy, so Jews can support themselves from their own land without needing help from each other or from other nations.

keyTerms.meaning: One who holds power, a ruler
To make a living, to be supported

steps.whatToRemember: The full prayer of the כהן גדול: if the year is hot, let it be rainy and moist; do not accept the prayer of travelers; may rulership stay with יהודה; may ישראל not depend on each other or on other nations for a living.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rava concludes
phrases.notes: Adds the closing lines of the prayer

phrases.english: in the name of Rav Yehuda:
may the one who rules not depart
phrases.notes: Language similar to בראשית מט:י

phrases.english: from the house of Judah,
and may Your people Israel not be
in need of being supported by one another,
nor by another nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְסַיֵּים מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the closing lines to the prayer quoted in Steps 33 and 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What were the words of the כהן גדול's short prayer?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Its closing lines: may rulership not leave יהודה, and may ישראל not depend on each other or on other nations for a living.

steps.title: A heavenly voice: the world is fed in רבי חנינא's merit, yet he lives on a little carob
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: every day a בת קול announces that the whole world is fed because of רבי חנינא בן דוסא, but he himself lives on one קב of carobs from one Friday to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Every single day a בת קול goes out and says: The whole world is fed because of My son חנינא, and for My son חנינא a קב of carobs is enough from one ערב שבת to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new section of stories praising רבי חנינא בן דוסא. It opens with a statement from רב about how great and how poor he was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a sharp contrast here. His merit brings food to the whole world, yet he lives on a tiny amount of cheap food. Carobs were simple, low-quality food, so this shows both his poverty and his contentment with little.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב (a small measure) of carobs

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Each and every day
a heavenly voice goes out and says:
The entire world is fed
because of My son Ḥanina,
phrases.notes: In his merit

phrases.english: and for My son Ḥanina a kav of carobs is enough
phrases.notes: A very small amount of simple food

phrases.english: from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.
phrases.notes: For a whole week

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prayer discussion to a new set of statements and stories about רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole world is fed in רבי חנינא בן דוסא's merit, yet he himself lives on one קב of carobs a week.

steps.title: A story begins: his wife heats the oven and makes smoke every Friday
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's wife would heat the oven every Friday and throw in material that made smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife used to heat the oven every ערב שבת and throw in something that made smoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story about רבי חנינא בן דוסא's wife. The story continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They had no food to bake. She made smoke so the neighbors would think she was baking for Shabbat, so the family's poverty would not be noticed. This connects to Step 36, which said he lived on almost nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: The story is not finished here. The point of the smoke is explained in the next lines of the גמרא.

phrases.english: His wife was accustomed
to heat the oven
every Shabbat eve
and to throw in smoke-making material
phrases.notes: So it would look as though she was baking

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that shows the poverty described in Step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup of a story: every Friday his wife heated an empty oven and made smoke.
